items.typical_cadential_gesture: II -> I: the major supertonic triad falling to the tonic keeps #4 in play and avoids the leading-tone pull of a real dominant.
items.character: Brightest diatonic mode; the raised fourth removes the tonic-defining tritone with 7 and replaces it with a tritone against the tonic itself.
items.notes: Do not harmonise #4 with a plain IV triad; that instantly re-reads the passage as the major scale of the subdominant.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: V7 -> I authentic cadence.
items.character: The reference bright mode. Functional rather than colouristic: its leading tone makes true cadences available.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: bVII -> I: the flat-seventh triad falling to the tonic is the mode's signature cadence.
items.character: Major third with a lowered seventh. Stable dominant-seventh tonic colour without any obligation to resolve.
items.notes: The natural 4 is a tension over the tonic chord; treat it as a passing or suspended tone rather than a chord member unless the profile wants sus harmony.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: IV -> i: the major subdominant triad falling to the minor tonic exposes the natural 6.
items.character: Minor mode with a raised sixth. The brightest of the common minor modes and the default modal-vamp colour for jazz, funk and neo-soul.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: bVII -> i or bVI -> bVII -> i.
items.character: The reference dark mode. Without a raised seventh it has no dominant of its own, which is exactly what makes it read as modal rather than tonal minor.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: bII -> i: the flat-second triad descending by step to the tonic (Phrygian cadence).
items.character: Very dark. The half step above the tonic is the whole identity of the mode and must be audible in the bass or the top voice.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: There is no stable cadence to a Locrian tonic; the mode is used as a chord scale over iiø7 rather than as a key.
items.character: Darkest diatonic mode and the only one whose tonic triad is diminished, so it cannot prolong a tonic without external support such as a pedal.
items.notes: Prefer locrian_natural_2 as the practical chord scale for a half-diminished chord, because b2 clashes with the chord root.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: V7 -> i with the raised sixth and seventh retained through the cadence.
items.character: Minor tonic with both upper degrees raised. In common practice the raised degrees are an ascending melodic device and the descending form reverts to natural minor; in jazz the collection is used in both directions as a fixed chord scale.
items.notes: Ascending-versus-descending interpretation: analysis treats a descending 6 and 7 as natural-minor degrees rather than a modulation, while generation over a minor-major seventh chord uses the fixed ascending collection.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: V7 -> i, with the augmented second between b6 and 7 handled by leaping only in inner voices or by filling it in.
items.character: Minor tonic with a real leading tone. Supplies the dominant that natural minor lacks, at the cost of an augmented second in the upper tetrachord.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: Used as a colour over a non-resolving or tritone-substitute dominant rather than as a cadential key.
items.character: Dominant seventh with a raised eleventh and a natural thirteenth. The default chord scale for a dominant that does not want to resolve down a fifth.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: V7alt -> I or i, with every altered tone resolving by step into the target chord.
items.character: Every tension above the guide tones is altered. Maximum instability, so it needs a destination; it is a resolution device, not a resting place.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: iiø7 -> V7alt -> i in minor.
items.character: Half-diminished chord scale with a natural ninth, which removes the b9 clash that plain Locrian creates against the chord root.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: V7b9 -> i, or the Andalusian descent bVII - bVI - V.
items.character: Major third over a Phrygian lower tetrachord. The dominant of harmonic minor treated as a mode in its own right.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: i - IV#11 - i vamp; the raised fourth is a colour, not a leading tone.
items.character: Dorian with a raised fourth. Reads as folk or cinematic minor rather than functional harmony.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: Prolonged by common tone rather than cadence; typically resolves upward by step from #5 to 6 into a plain major chord.
items.character: Brightest collection in common use: both the fourth and the fifth are raised, so the tonic chord is an augmented major seventh.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: V7b13 -> i in minor.
items.character: Dominant colour with a flat thirteenth. The standard chord scale for a dominant resolving to a minor tonic.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: No cadential obligation; the collection has no half steps and therefore no tendency tones.
items.character: Five-note major subset with the fourth and seventh removed, which deletes every half step and every avoid note.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: No cadential obligation; used over static minor or dominant vamps.
items.character: Five-note minor subset. Freely usable over minor seventh, dominant seventh and suspended harmony because it contains no leading tone.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: Cadence is rhetorical rather than functional: the b3 and b5 bend into 3 and 5 over a stable dominant-seventh tonic.
items.character: Minor pentatonic plus the flat fifth used as a passing inflection. Deliberately conflicts with the major third of the underlying dominant chords, which is the point.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: Slides chromatically into a target chord; it has no internal cadence because every step is identical.
items.character: Fully symmetric, so it has no tonic and only two transpositions. Used for suspension of tonal gravity.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: Resolves down a fifth like any dominant; the symmetry supplies four possible roots.
items.character: Alternating half and whole steps starting with a half step. Supplies b9, #9, #11 and natural 13 over a dominant chord simultaneously.

items.typical_cadential_gesture: Any of its four diminished-seventh chords can resolve up by half step; the spelling chosen must reflect the intended destination.
items.character: Alternating whole and half steps. The scale of the fully diminished seventh chord and of common-tone diminished motion.
